label: POST HOC hand coding by the conductor (an instance of the makers' family), after the results were seen. It replaces the regex in posthoc.py part A, which counted 'nothing from what I already knew' as declared knowledge. One coder, once.

codes.used: the maker says the words, or a load-bearing word, came from a known rendering
codes.avoided: the maker names a known rendering and says it did not use it
codes.shaped: the maker does not say it avoided a rendering, but says its knowledge shaped the choice (metre, stress, greeting, which sounds count)
codes.picture: the maker says the words came from the picture, and names no rendering it knew

notes.U1c: Named the song Golden-crowned Sparrow (confidence 40) and wrote 'oh dear me', which is that species' published rendering (All About Birds photo-gallery caption: https://www.allaboutbirds.org/guide/Golden-crowned_Sparrow/photo-gallery/297970171 ; Audubon field guide: https://prelaunch.audubon.org/field-guide/bird/golden-crowned-sparrow). The song is a White-throated Sparrow's. A wrong placement carried the wrong tracing. P6 is void by its letter (confidence under 50).
notes.U4c: Coded picture: the maker names a tune it avoided ('Three Blind Mice'), not a rendering of the bird.
notes.N2g: 'BEER' is half of the published 'free-beer!'; the committed marker rule (`free beer`, `beep`) did not match it, so P3 counts it as no return. Recorded, not re-scored.
notes.N1c: Avoided the triplet renderings on the picture's evidence ('this cut has no triplets') but kept 'sweet' and says so.
notes.ovenbird: Four makers who recognised or were told Ovenbird avoided 'teacher' and all four kept its metre: cheaper x8 (U2), PICK-up x8 (U3), Peter x9 (N2), sister x8 (N3). No word shared, one metre.
